args.title: Direct delivery now requires an episode record before the pulse can end
args.body:
The sealed rejection replay (evidence/rejection/) ended with delivered:false, recorded:[], offers:0 in both arms even after commits 91b5bc0 and e088110. Re-reading the transcript shows the remaining gap: the pulse did mention DELIVER, but only after the direct-head explanation and a session-level CHECKPOINT. A resumed session could therefore preserve the work as a Git commit and stop without any episode record; the next session sees the journal, not that commit.

Root cause: the continuity summary computed the formal Work next action (including CHECKPOINT) first, then appended an optional DELIVER sentence. The first legal command in nextActions.mechanical was not DELIVER, and there was no requiredAction field at the top of the pulse. Advice alone did not make the unrecorded state visible as the one missing operation.

Fix in commit cd6ef14d708c: for a clean taskless project with a direct commit ahead of the canonical basis, the summary computes RECORD/REUSE before the formal action. RECORD emits a structural `requiredAction` (kind RECORD_DIRECT_DELIVERY, repositoryHead, reason) at the top of the pulse and makes the DELIVER command the first mechanical action; CHECKPOINT and the optional "propose the next step" are withheld. REUSE points at the current recorded conclusion instead. Dirty worktrees, unchanged repositories, formal tasks, attempts and promotion facts keep their existing guidance. The field is propagated through ProjectPulse and the tool description tells the next turn to perform it before replying.

Verification: new independent oracle `node scripts/pnwf/software/self-maintenance-delivery-required.mjs` passes 10/10 on cd6ef14. Replayed against e088110, the same oracle fails: firstCommand is `conclude intent=CHECKPOINT`, requiredAction is null, delivery is REFUSED, and no episode entry exists. The earlier pulse oracle still passes 7/7, the readiness oracle 6/6, and the nine related suites pass 66/66. This is an advisory direct deliverable: it records no operator acceptance, promotion or canonical-head advance.

args.title: Direct delivery now requires an episode record before the pulse can end
args.body:
The sealed rejection replay (evidence/rejection/) ended with delivered:false, recorded:[], offers:0 in both arms even after commits 91b5bc0 and e088110. Re-reading the transcript shows the remaining gap: the pulse did mention DELIVER, but only after the direct-head explanation and a session-level CHECKPOINT. A resumed session could therefore preserve the work as a Git commit and stop without any episode record; the next session sees the journal, not that commit.

Root cause: the continuity summary computed the formal Work next action (including CHECKPOINT) first, then appended an optional DELIVER sentence. The first legal command in nextActions.mechanical was not DELIVER, and there was no requiredAction field at the top of the pulse. Advice alone did not make the unrecorded state visible as the one missing operation.

Fix in commit cd6ef14d708c: for a clean taskless project with a direct commit ahead of the canonical basis, the summary computes RECORD/REUSE before the formal action. RECORD emits a structural `requiredAction` (kind RECORD_DIRECT_DELIVERY, repositoryHead, reason) at the top of the pulse and makes the DELIVER command the first mechanical action; CHECKPOINT and the optional "propose the next step" are withheld. REUSE points at the current recorded conclusion instead. Dirty worktrees, unchanged repositories, formal tasks, attempts and promotion facts keep their existing guidance. The field is propagated through ProjectPulse and the tool description tells the next turn to perform it before replying.

Verification: new independent oracle `node scripts/pnwf/software/self-maintenance-delivery-required.mjs` passes 10/10 on cd6ef14. Replayed against e088110, the same oracle fails: firstCommand is `conclude intent=CHECKPOINT`, requiredAction is null, delivery is REFUSED, and no episode entry exists. The earlier pulse oracle still passes 7/7, the readiness oracle 6/6, and the nine related suites pass 66/66. This is an advisory direct deliverable: it records no operator acceptance, promotion or canonical-head advance.
